bullets.title: MRVL: Investor Day raises FY28 to $20B, FY31 guide $70-90B; broad PT upgrades
bullets.body: Marvell's Oct 6 Investor Day was a major catalyst. The company raised FY28 revenue guidance from ~$18B to $20B and introduced a FY31 framework of $70-90B revenue with >$30 EPS (~55-60% CAGR), well above FactSet consensus of $47B. Custom silicon target lifted to $12B+ in FY29 vs prior $10B, with interconnect expected to contribute $37.5B by FY31. Stock rallied ~8% intraday. Buy-side upgrades poured in: Piper to $400 (18x FY31), TD Cowen to $350 (from $245, new Buy), Wolfe to $375, UBS to $350, JPM to $360, Roth to $350. MRVL now confirmed as custom silicon supplier for all four major cloud hyperscalers including new Google agreement.

bullets.title: LITE/AAOI: Lumentum sold out through early 2029 on AI optical demand; AAOI best-risk-reward play
bullets.body: Lumentum CEO confirmed optical components are completely sold out through early 2029, unable to meet ~70% of 2027 demand and ~30% of 2028 demand for some products. Stock hit 52-week highs (+567% YTD). Sympathy moves: AAOI, COHR, TSEM, GLW, CIEN, FN all gained. Wolfe is long AAOI into OCP conference (Oct 13-15), citing 4x EV/sales 2027 discount and >200% growth potential; short FORM on CPO delay thesis. Citi ranks ANET #1 and LITE #2 networking picks as Big-5 cloud capex growth revised higher to +93% YoY for 2026.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 Pro orders cut 15-20% in October on soft demand; PC market -20% YoY
bullets.body: Apple instructed suppliers to cut iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max component orders by at least 15% for October due to weak demand after a $100+ price increase. KeyBanc estimates ~52.8M units in F4Q vs consensus 57.8M. PC shipments fell 20.1% YoY in 3Q to 62.7M units—HP down 30.9%, Dell down 25%, Apple down 11.3% (but Apple gained 90bps share). Wolfe notes SWKS (~60% Apple revenue) and QRVO (~50%) are most at risk from the cuts.

bullets.title: T/VZ/TMUS: SpaceX $8B 800MHz spectrum buy signals fourth carrier threat; tower stocks surge
bullets.body: SpaceX acquired a nationwide 800MHz spectrum portfolio from Grain Management for ~$8B, positioning Starlink Mobile as a potential terrestrial carrier. T fell ~10%, VZ ~10%, TMUS ~12% on the week with heavy put buying. Tower stocks (CCI +18%, SBAC +14%) surged as SpaceX will need tower infrastructure for ~60-70K macro sites. Citi is a buyer of SBAC, AMT, CCI; MS models <1% US mobile penetration by 2030 scaling to ~7% by 2035. AT&T separately announced a fiber JV with GIP/CPP Investments (50% AT&T stake) combining Forged Fiber 37 and Gigapower targeting 60M addresses by 2030.

bullets.title: CEG/GOOGL: 20-year 890MW nuclear deal plus 2.7GW PPA; IPPs rally ~15%
bullets.body: Constellation Energy and Google confirmed a 20-year PPA for 890MW of new nuclear capacity in PJM plus a 15-year agreement for an additional 2.7GW. The deal represents $4.3B+ in Constellation investments across 11 nuclear units; first uprate expected by 2028. Morgan Stanley estimates ~$2.50/share EPS upside and ~$800M incremental FCF for CEG. IPPs (CEG, VST, TLN) rallied ~15% on average as data-center power contracting at incumbent PJM assets accelerates without 1-for-1 new generation requirements.

bullets.title: NFLX: 5% workforce RIF expected; MS reiterate OW at $80 PT on DD revenue growth and margin expansion
bullets.body: Netflix is preparing a ~5% workforce restructuring (~850 employees), expected to be announced as early as next week. Despite this, Morgan Stanley reiterates Overweight at $80 PT (from $83), citing double-digit revenue growth and 150-200bps annual margin expansion potential. Ad revenue forecast to triple to $4.8B by 2027. Engagement data (top-10 viewing -11% YoY) and streaming share declines remain overhangs. Wolfe downgraded the stock on engagement challenges.

bullets.title: PLTR: Goldman upgrades to Buy, $230 PT on sovereign AI TAM step-change
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs upgraded Palantir to Buy from Neutral with a $230 PT (+18%), citing a step-function TAM change via sovereign AI/verticalization strategy. PLTR's FDE model with AI automation sustains competitive moat; revenue estimates rise materially from 2027 onward. PLTR +10.75% intraday mid-week was among Nasdaq leadership. Separately, Wolfe Research is bullish into earnings and sees large-order wave buying in CRWD as extending.

bullets.title: META: Muse AI agent #1 app for 22 days; $27B+ revenue potential per Citi; OTA/marketplace selloff overdone
bullets.body: Meta's Muse personal AI agent maintained the #1 US App Store ranking for 22 consecutive days with 6.6M+ downloads and 1.8M DAUs. Citi raised META to Buy with $800 PT, projecting Muse could generate $27B+ revenue at scale via transaction monetization (~5% take rate on $170B volume in year 1). Amazon blocked Muse from its platform. OTA stocks (BKNG, ABNB, EXPE) fell 15-25% on agentic AI fears but Wolfe sees risk as overdone—only 27% of consumers have tried Muse and 64% won't trust agents with credit cards. META banned ByteDance advertising in 7 countries.

bullets.title: NOW/MSFT/SNOW/NET: JPM favors all four into 3Q earnings; downgrades HUBS
bullets.body: JPMorgan flags NOW (cRPO beat likely ~200bps, AI ACV target raise expected), MSFT (10M+ Copilot seat adds, modest M365 upside), SNOW (accelerated migration pace, further acceleration in F4Q27), and NET (high-30% revenue growth from Workers and AI demand) as its top software longs. HUBS is downgraded to Neutral—AI monetization delayed, medium-term revenue growth at risk; the stock also announced a 7% workforce RIF (~660 employees). KeyBanc NOW partner call shows all renewing customers migrating to new AI SKUs with 10-25% spend uplift.

bullets.title: ACN: F4Q26 beats consensus by ~300bps; UBS and Mizuho raise PTs ahead of Oct 14 Analyst Day
bullets.body: Accenture delivered F4Q26 CC revenue growth of +7% YoY vs +1-5% guidance, with new bookings re-accelerating to +5% CC YoY. ~100 new clients started advanced AI work in the quarter; emerging AI partner bookings tripled YoY. FY27 guidance of +3-6% CC revenue growth modestly above expectations. Mizuho raises PT to $241 (from $226, Outperform); UBS maintains Buy at $275. Trump administration also suspended MSFT, ACN, CTSH, and others from H-1B PERM program (ACN +5.96% intraday on the news as it removes offshore labor overhang).

bullets.title: TSM: September revenue +54.6% YoY at record NT$1.49tn; capex raised to $85B in 2027
bullets.body: TSMC September revenue beat consensus by ~3% on AI chip demand. GS and UBS raised FY26 revenue to +40-mid-40s% guidance. 2027 capex estimates raised to $85B (UBS, from $78B) and $98B in 2028. N3 capacity remains tight; N2 ramp on track. Separately, Musk confirmed TSLA/SpaceX Terafab fab will be built and run by his companies; TSMC could only sublease a portion. TSMC is also evaluating a second US fab cluster in Texas potentially exceeding $265B in total investment.

bullets.title: GOOGL: TPU Anthropic revenue could add $50-100B EBIT by 2028; Gemini Agent launched; $400 PT
bullets.body: JPMorgan flags GOOGL as an under-appreciated AI infrastructure monetization story: TPU sales to Anthropic could reach 10GW by 2028 generating $50-100B EBIT vs. Street 2028 EBIT of $270B. Morgan Stanley reiterates OW at $400, citing Waymo as key agentic AI differentiator (forecast ~$21B revenue by 2032). GOOGL also launched Gemini Agent for enterprise with multi-model orchestration. Prediction markets now show Google overtaking Anthropic in AI model leadership (43% vs 42%). Separately, GOOGL faces privacy concerns from 120+ lawmakers over its planned acquisition of Spirit Airlines passenger data for AI training.

bullets.title: AMD: PT raised to $705-800 on agentic AI CPU TAM; plans substantial 2027 supply increase
bullets.body: Citi raised AMD to $800 PT (from prior level) citing agentic AI driving CPU TAM from $29B in 2025 to $300B by 2030 (~60% CAGR). AMD is the primary CPU beneficiary as Meta is one of its largest server customers. Mizuho also raised AMD to $705 (from $580). AMD CEO Lisa Su confirmed plans to 'substantially increase' chip supply in 2027 and said demand is 'very high for several years.' AMD also acquired World Labs for ~$8.2B in all-stock to expand physical AI/robotics capabilities.

bullets.title: MU: Record Q4, $600M Netlist settlement; 2027-28 supply significantly tighter than 2026
bullets.body: Micron delivered record Q4 revenue of $54.2B with profit up >1,000%; 75% of 2027 output already allocated. HBM pricing expected to roughly double from HBM3E to HBM4. Company settled with Netlist for $600M ($30M/quarter over 5 years) covering server DIMMs and HBM patents. Management guided FY27 capex raised to $50B+. Taiwan union authorized strike over bonus dispute (99% vote), though timing remains uncertain. DA Davidson raised PT to $3,000; supply/demand expected tight through CY28.

bullets.title: SHOP: JPM raises PT to $200 on agentic commerce positioning; 30% 2027 revenue growth path
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised Shopify PT to $200 (Dec-27) from $185, reiterating Overweight and top pick. Agentic commerce is a structural positive: Shop Pay integrated into Meta Muse and OpenAI ChatGPT, converting ~2x vs traditional channels. SHOP delivered five consecutive quarters of 30%+ GMV/revenue growth. JPM models ~27% 2027 revenue growth with FCF margins of ~20%. SHOP's platform approach—owning channels, on-platform AI (Sidekick), and infrastructure—gives multiple monetization layers as AI agents reshape commerce.

bullets.title: HUT/WULF/CORZ/DLR/EQIX: Data center build-out themes dominate; Jefferies bullish on supply/demand
bullets.body: Jefferies' data center PTO model forecasts 12.9 GW new capacity 2026, 18 GW 2027, and 26 GW 2028 with ~33% growth in 2026 accelerating to mid-30s. DLR and EQIX each own ~3 GW in highest-imbalance markets and are well-positioned for rent growth. Former Bitcoin miners (CORZ, HUT, WULF) offer AI data center lease upside. UBS survey finds broad investor agreement on AI/HPC colocation sector—WULF top pick for execution/valuation. HUT's River Bend Phase 1 (330MW) is on time/budget with Phase 2 expansion path visible; MS and Roth both flag as Buy.

bullets.title: ANET: Citi initiates Buy at $248 PT; Etherlink SU-144 unlocks $10B scale-up networking TAM
bullets.body: Citi initiated Arista Networks at Buy with a $248 PT (36x 2028 EPS, 17.6% upside). Arista launched Etherlink SU-144, a pure Ethernet scale-up solution competing with NVDA's NVLink; the ESUN standard is imminent with a $10B 2027 TAM per Dell'Oro. MSFT is collaborating on Maia accelerators; META on scale-out. JPM also revised their AI DC switch TAM higher—Arista holds 20% share (down from 22% Q1), with CLS and CSCO closing the gap. ANET is Citi's #1 networking pick.

bullets.title: SPOT: Piper initiates Neutral $540; Citi Buy $620 on audiobooks; Rogan deal renewed at ~$250M
bullets.body: Spotify confirmed a new multi-year deal with Joe Rogan estimated at ~$250M on similar prior terms. Spotify also expanded audiobooks to 180+ markets (750M+ users eligible), which Citi flags as a meaningful 2027 gross margin tailwind (~€0.10 ARPU uplift in new markets). Citi maintains Buy with $620 PT (27x 2027E FCF). Piper Sandler initiated at Neutral with $540 PT, noting ad business rebuild headwinds and lower CPMs. Wolfe cuts SPOT gross margin to 33.6% vs 33.9% consensus.

bullets.title: INTC/TSM Terafab: Musk confirms Tesla/SpaceX will build and run fab; INTC remains development partner
bullets.body: Elon Musk clarified that Tesla and SpaceX will build and operate the Terafab AI chip facility; TSMC could only sublease a portion and will not operate as an equal partner. Intel CEO confirmed Intel remains an active manufacturing partner for Terafab via the 14A process ($16.8B initial investment, up to $119B total). INTC fell ~12.3% on the week—the market interpreted the Terafab development as removing INTC as a primary beneficiary. INTC will continue working with Musk but its role is narrower than initially implied.

bullets.title: DIS: Wolfe raises PT to $132; MS reiterates OW on NFLX DIS deal and India growth
bullets.body: Wolfe raised Disney PT to $132 (from $131), citing ~$300M in annual cost savings being reinvested into DTC growth; stock trades at 14x FY27 EPS (~10% discount to S&P), which Wolfe calls too attractive. Morgan Stanley reiterates Overweight on NFLX ($80 PT) noting the DIS licensing deal (all 5 Ice Age films) and India streaming green shoots as catalysts. MS also initiated Disney at OW via Yorkville Ives at $125 PT. The PSKY-WBD merger closed on October 6, creating SKYD.
